initiatives.name: Barratt-Redrow Acquisition and Integration
initiatives.summary: The Group continued integrating Barratt Developments and Redrow plc throughout FY26, aligning governance, risk management, internal control frameworks and culture across the combined business. The RCF was also amended and extended to reflect the increased scale of the Group following the acquisition.

evidence.title: Procurement synergies from Redrow acquisition
evidence.summary: The company estimates the Redrow acquisition will deliver £39m of total procurement synergies, with £20m already captured and the remainder expected before December 2027. This is part of broader cost synergy realization from combining supply chains.
evidence.quote: In addition, we estimate that the acquisition of Redrow will deliver a total of £39m of procurement synergies with £20m captured to date, and the outstanding synergies to be achieved before December 2027.

evidence.title: Multi-branding synergy sales outlets programme
evidence.summary: Following the Redrow acquisition, the company identified 45 opportunities to add additional sales outlets through multi-branding across combined developments, opening 12 in FY26 with 18 planned for FY27 and 15 for FY28, to improve asset turn and return on capital.
evidence.quote: With the Redrow acquisition, we immediately identified 45 opportunities across our combined developments to add additional sales outlets to deliver revenue synergies... This supports our outlet opening programme, with 12 new outlets opened in FY26 and a further 18 planned in FY27.

evidence.title: Synergy cost savings from Barratt-Redrow combination
evidence.summary: The Group is targeting incremental cost synergies from the combination, with procurement-based cost synergies and incremental savings within adjusted profit before tax guided for FY27. Cumulative synergy savings are tracked against a £95m target.
evidence.quote: Synergy cost savings Incremental c. £22m within adjusted profit before tax (£95m cumulative)

evidence.title: Integration of Barratt and Redrow following acquisition
evidence.summary: The Group continued integrating Barratt Developments and Redrow plc throughout FY26, aligning governance, risk management, internal control frameworks and culture across the combined business. The RCF was also amended and extended to reflect the increased scale of the Group following the acquisition.
evidence.quote: Most notably, the year has been characterised by the continued integration of Barratt Developments and Redrow following the combination of our businesses. The Board devoted considerable time and attention to overseeing the integration programme, ensuring that it is progressing in a disciplined and value-accretive manner.

evidence.title: New CFO Rebecca Napier appointed to replace Mike Scott
evidence.summary: Following the departure of CFO Mike Scott, the Board appointed Rebecca Napier as Chief Financial Officer after a comprehensive search process, with incoming CEO Dean Banks consulted on the decision. She is expected to support disciplined capital allocation and delivery of synergies from the Redrow combination.
evidence.quote: Rebecca's appointment was announced on 19 June 2026.

evidence.title: Redrow acquisition integration and synergy delivery
evidence.summary: Barratt completed the operational integration of Redrow during FY26, including divisional office network consolidation, restructuring of Group support functions, and IT integration. Total expected cost synergies of £100m were confirmed, with £73m delivered to date and the remainder expected by HY28.
evidence.quote: The divisional office network, the restructuring of Group support functions and IT integration have all been completed and total expected cost synergies of £100m have been confirmed. We delivered incremental cost synergies of £53m in the year, ahead of our original plan.

initiatives.name: Zero Carbon Homes Development Roadmap
initiatives.summary: The company proactively adopted provisions of the Future Homes Standard (confirmed March 2026) ahead of regulatory requirements, including air source heat pumps becoming standard and assessing solar PV feasibility, to comply with new carbon emission requirements for new homes by March 2027.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £10,200 estimated additional capital cost per house (HBF estimate)

evidence.title: HVO fuel substitution driving Scope 1 and 2 emissions reduction
evidence.summary: The Group significantly increased the proportion of diesel substituted with HVO (hydrotreated vegetable oil) fuel, a key driver in reducing operational carbon emissions by 40.2% compared to the FY25 baseline.
evidence.quote: Scope 1 and 2 emissions fell by 40.2% compared to 2025, primarily driven by increasing the proportion of diesel substituted with HVO from 39% in FY25 to 87% in FY26.

evidence.title: Future Homes Standard compliance preparation
evidence.summary: The company proactively adopted provisions of the Future Homes Standard (confirmed March 2026) ahead of regulatory requirements, including air source heat pumps becoming standard and assessing solar PV feasibility, to comply with new carbon emission requirements for new homes by March 2027.
evidence.quote: With the FHS consultation having launched in December 2023, we acted quickly to adopt many of the proposed provisions in advance, and they will be standard for our new house type range. Air source heat pumps are being adopted across our developments and the next steps will be to assess PV feasibility on our roof layouts.

evidence.title: Zero carbon homes roadmap via eHome2 and innovation partnerships
evidence.summary: The Group is investing in research collaborations, prototype homes (eHome²), fleet electrification and customer insights to deliver zero carbon homes by 2030, aiming for a sustainable cost advantage and reputational benefit ahead of regulation.
evidence.quote: We invest in innovation, trials and partnerships to deliver zero carbon homes by 2030. Our roadmap includes research collaborations, reducing reliance on fuel, electrifying our fleet, prototype homes such as eHome² and customer insights.

initiatives.name: Capital Return and Share Buyback Programme FY27
initiatives.summary: The Board announced a total capital return of £400m for FY27, with approximately £386m returned through a share buyback programme (commenced 15 July 2026) and the remainder through a nominal dividend. This reflects optimized capital allocation given shares trading at a discount to tangible net asset value.

evidence.title: £400m capital return and share buyback programme FY27
evidence.summary: The Board announced a total capital return of £400m for FY27, with approximately £386m returned through a share buyback programme (commenced 15 July 2026) and the remainder through a nominal dividend. This reflects optimized capital allocation given shares trading at a discount to tangible net asset value.
evidence.quote: For FY27, the Board has therefore announced a total capital return of £400m. Approximately £386m will be returned through a share buyback programme, which commenced on 15 July 2026; £53.5m has been returned as at 6 September 2026.

evidence.title: Revised capital allocation framework and share buyback programme
evidence.summary: The Board updated its capital allocation framework, announced in a trading update, reducing ordinary dividends in favor of share buybacks as the preferred method of returning capital to shareholders. A share buyback of approximately £386m is planned to be completed by July 2027.
evidence.quote: The update to our capital allocation framework announced in our trading update on 15 July 2026 is summarised in the "Using capital effectively" section of the CEO Review on page 20.

initiatives.name: Administrative Cost Reduction and Recruitment Freeze
initiatives.summary: During FY26, the company implemented a freeze on recruitment (other than essential role replacement) alongside disciplined cost management, resulting in a significant reduction in adjusted administrative expenses compared to prior year levels.

evidence.title: Recruitment freeze and administrative cost reduction
evidence.summary: During FY26, the company implemented a freeze on recruitment (other than essential role replacement) alongside disciplined cost management, resulting in a significant reduction in adjusted administrative expenses compared to prior year levels.
evidence.quote: During FY26 this has involved a freeze on recruitment, other than essential role replacement and other costs. The combination of Redrow cost synergies and our disciplined approach to costs has resulted in a reduction in our adjusted administrative expenses of £68.7m when compared to our annualised expenses of £398.5m in FY25.

initiatives.name: RCF Refinancing and Facility Expansion
initiatives.summary: In July 2026, the Group refinanced its Revolving Credit Facility, increasing the facility size by £200m to £900m, reflecting strong banking relationships and supporting liquidity headroom and financial flexibility.

evidence.title: RCF refinancing with increased facility size
evidence.summary: In July 2026, the Group refinanced its Revolving Credit Facility, increasing the facility size by £200m to £900m, reflecting strong banking relationships and supporting liquidity headroom and financial flexibility.
evidence.quote: In July 2026, the Group successfully refinanced its Revolving Credit Facility (RCF), reflecting the strength of its relationships with core banking partners... The refinancing saw an increase to the facility size of £200m, with the Group now holding an RCF of £900m.

initiatives.name: Net Zero and Science-Based Emissions Targets
initiatives.summary: The Group updated its near-term and long-term greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets following the Barratt-Redrow combination, validated by the Science Based Targets initiative, committing to net zero across the value chain by 2045 with interim targets of 46.4% reduction in Scope 1&2 by 2035.

evidence.title: Net zero transition plan with science-based targets
evidence.summary: The Group updated its near-term and long-term greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets following the Barratt-Redrow combination, validated by the Science Based Targets initiative, committing to net zero across the value chain by 2045 with interim targets of 46.4% reduction in Scope 1&2 by 2035.
evidence.quote: We are committed to reaching net zero carbon across our value chain by 2045, with a structured approach to reducing Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions. In 2026, the Group updated its near-term and long-term greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets following the combination of Barratt and Redrow.

evidence.title: Updated science-based GHG emissions reduction targets post-combination
evidence.summary: Following the Barratt-Redrow combination, the Group updated its near-term and long-term greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets, validated by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), committing to net zero by FY2045 and specific interim reduction targets by FY2035.
evidence.quote: Barratt Redrow plc commits to achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions across the value chain by FY2045. Near-term Barratt Redrow plc commits to reduce absolute scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions 46.4% by FY2035 from a FY2025 base year.

initiatives.name: Building Safety Remediation Programme
initiatives.summary: The company has a dedicated Building Safety team responsible for identifying and executing remediation works at historic developments, recognizing additional costs of £103.1m in FY26 relating to legacy building safety issues, as part of compliance with Building Safety Self-Remediation Terms signed in March 2023.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £103.1m additional remediation costs in FY26; £96.8m legacy property charges

evidence.title: Building Safety remediation programme and dedicated team
evidence.summary: The company has a dedicated Building Safety team responsible for identifying and executing remediation works at historic developments, recognizing additional costs of £103.1m in FY26 relating to legacy building safety issues, as part of compliance with Building Safety Self-Remediation Terms signed in March 2023.
evidence.quote: We are committed to progressing solutions as quickly as we are able and have a dedicated Building Safety team which is responsible for identifying required remediation works at our historic developments and ensuring that proposed and completed works meet with the approval of the Building Safety Regulator.

initiatives.name: Graduate and Apprenticeship Programme Expansion
initiatives.summary: The company expanded participation in its graduate, apprenticeship and trainee programmes to 526 participants in FY26 (up from 465 in FY25), representing approximately 7% of the workforce, including four degree apprenticeship programmes with Sheffield Hallam University.

evidence.title: Graduate, apprenticeship and trainee programme expansion
evidence.summary: The company expanded participation in its graduate, apprenticeship and trainee programmes to 526 participants in FY26 (up from 465 in FY25), representing approximately 7% of the workforce, including four degree apprenticeship programmes with Sheffield Hallam University.
evidence.quote: In total, our apprenticeship and degree programmes supported 526 participants as at 28 June 2026 (FY25: 465), representing c.7% (FY25: c.6%) of our workforce, highlighting our commitment to future talent development.

evidence.title: Workforce engagement and talent initiatives amid leadership transition
evidence.summary: The Group has invested in apprenticeships, graduate development, training academies, succession planning and a relaunched set of Group values to attract and retain talent amid competition for skills, particularly important given the scale of leadership change during FY26.
evidence.quote: Apprenticeships, graduate development, training academies and development programmes. Group-wide succession planning and personal development plans for all employees. Group values relaunched and embedded.

initiatives.name: Competition Appeal Tribunal Class Action
initiatives.summary: A proposed collective action was filed against seven housebuilders, including Barratt Redrow, alleging anti-competitive information sharing that led to higher prices, following a closed CMA investigation that accepted binding commitments from the housebuilders.

evidence.title: Competition Appeal Tribunal class action against housebuilders
evidence.summary: A proposed collective action was filed against seven housebuilders, including Barratt Redrow, alleging anti-competitive information sharing that led to higher prices, following a closed CMA investigation that accepted binding commitments from the housebuilders.
evidence.quote: On 24 June 2026 an application to commence proposed collective action was filed in the Competition Appeal Tribunal, against seven housebuilders, including Barratt Redrow, alleging that exchanges of competitively sensitive information reduced competition and led to higher prices for certain purchasers of new build homes, in breach of UK competition law.

initiatives.name: MADE Partnership Master Developer Joint Venture
initiatives.summary: Established in September 2024, the MADE Partnership is a joint venture between Barratt Redrow, Homes England, and Lloyds Banking Group to unlock complex, large-scale residential communities. Six developments with capacity for more than 18,000 homes are being progressed, with Godley Green Garden Village the most advanced.

Six developments with capacity for more than 18,000 homes are being progressed, with Godley Green Garden Village the most advanced.
evidence.quote: Established in September 2024, the MADE Partnership is a master developer joint venture between Barratt Redrow plc, Homes England, and Lloyds Banking Group to unlock and deliver complex, large-scale residential communities. initiatives.name: External Audit Tender and EY Appointment
initiatives.summary: The Audit and Risk Committee completed a competitive external audit tender process during FY26, holding an additional dedicated Committee meeting to assess participating firms, ultimately recommending EY for appointment as the Group's new auditor.

evidence.title: External audit tender process completed - EY recommended

initiatives.name: CEO Leadership Transition
initiatives.summary: Following the planned retirement of long-serving CEO David Thomas, the Board appointed Dean Banks as Group Chief Executive Officer after a comprehensive succession process led by the Nomination and Governance Committee with external search adviser Russell Reynolds. The appointment is intended to bring new strategic vision to lead the enlarged Group following the Redrow combination.

evidence.title: New CEO Dean Banks appointed following David Thomas retirement
evidence.summary: Following the planned retirement of long-serving CEO David Thomas, the Board appointed Dean Banks as Group Chief Executive Officer after a comprehensive succession process led by the Nomination and Governance Committee with external search adviser Russell Reynolds. The appointment is intended to bring new strategic vision to lead the enlarged Group following the Redrow combination.
evidence.quote: Following its assessment, the Committee recommended the appointment of Dean Banks as Chief Executive Officer, which the Board approved and announced on 4 March 2026.

initiatives.name: Gilston Joint Venture with Places for People
initiatives.summary: In April 2026, Barratt Redrow formed a joint venture with Places for People to deliver 8,500 homes at Gilston, East Hertfordshire, including 1,950 affordable homes and supporting infrastructure like schools and health centres.

evidence.quote: In April 2026, we formed a joint venture with Places for People to deliver 8,500 homes at Gilston, East Hertfordshire, in one of the UK's most significant placemaking projects of recent years.

initiatives.name: Placemaking Operational Framework
initiatives.summary: The Group approved a new Placemaking Operational Framework integrating best practice across the development lifecycle, embedding customer-focused design, supporting consistency across the combined business while allowing brand differentiation, to be enhanced with post-occupancy evaluation.

evidence.title: New Placemaking Operational Framework approved
evidence.summary: The Group approved a new Placemaking Operational Framework integrating best practice across the development lifecycle, embedding customer-focused design, supporting consistency across the combined business while allowing brand differentiation, to be enhanced with post-occupancy evaluation.
evidence.quote: The Committee approved a new Placemaking Operational Framework, integrating best practice across the development lifecycle and aligning with national planning policy.

evidence.title: RSPB biodiversity partnership supporting placemaking
evidence.summary: The Group has an ongoing partnership with the RSPB on biodiversity initiatives, which contributes to placemaking goals and customer outcomes, reviewed as part of the newly approved Placemaking Operational Framework.
evidence.quote: The Committee reviewed progress on biodiversity initiatives, including the Group's partnership with the RSPB, recognising their contribution to placemaking and customer outcomes.

initiatives.name: Oregon Timber Frame Vertical Integration
initiatives.summary: The company has invested in selective vertical integration through Oregon, its wholly owned timber frame business, allowing flexibility to switch production methods quickly in response to construction input cost movements. In FY26, 5,558 home completions used timber frame construction.

evidence.title: Vertical integration through Oregon timber frame business
evidence.summary: The company has invested in selective vertical integration through Oregon, its wholly owned timber frame business, allowing flexibility to switch production methods quickly in response to construction input cost movements. In FY26, 5,558 home completions used timber frame construction.
evidence.quote: We have also invested in selective vertical integration opportunities. Through Oregon, our wholly owned timber frame business, we have the flexibility to switch production methods quickly, should we see more significant movements in traditional construction input costs.

initiatives.name: Timber Frame and SUDs Adoption for Climate Resilience
initiatives.summary: The Group increased use of timber frame construction and sustainable drainage systems (SUDs) to enhance build resilience and efficiency in response to weather disruption risks, alongside completing a detailed assessment of climate impacts on construction productivity.

evidence.title: Timber frame construction and SUDs adoption for climate resilience
evidence.summary: The Group increased use of timber frame construction and sustainable drainage systems (SUDs) to enhance build resilience and efficiency in response to weather disruption risks, alongside completing a detailed assessment of climate impacts on construction productivity.
evidence.quote: In FY26, 68% of projects included SUDs or flood protection, and 5,558 homes used timber frames to enhance resilience and build efficiency.

initiatives.name: Streamlined House Type Designs Across Brands

initiatives.name: Mauer Engineered Façade System Trial
initiatives.summary: The company is trialling alternative construction production methods including the Mauer engineered façade system, a lightweight brick facade printed onto calcium silicate board, which reduces need for skilled labour and reduces embodied carbon by c.50% compared to clay bricks. Currently trialled at Hollygate Green, Cotgrave, Nottinghamshire.

evidence.title: Trial of Mauer engineered façade system (MMC)
evidence.summary: The company is trialling alternative construction production methods including the Mauer engineered façade system, a lightweight brick facade printed onto calcium silicate board, which reduces need for skilled labour and reduces embodied carbon by c.50% compared to clay bricks. Currently trialled at Hollygate Green, Cotgrave, Nottinghamshire.
evidence.quote: We are trialling other alternative production methods including the Mauer engineered façade system, a lightweight brick facade which is printed onto a calcium silicate board and can be applied to timber frame and masonry external walls. This delivers a high‑quality finish, reducing the need for skilled labour, and reduces embodied carbon by c. 50% compared to clay bricks and mortar.

initiatives.name: Tutbury Park Flagship Sustainable Development
initiatives.summary: Tutbury Park near Burton-on-Trent is being developed as a flagship for sustainable living, featuring carbon-positive operational energy homes using learnings from University of Salford research including Energy House 2.0 and Zed House concept homes.

evidence.title: Tutbury Park flagship sustainable living development
evidence.summary: Tutbury Park near Burton-on-Trent is being developed as a flagship for sustainable living, featuring carbon-positive operational energy homes using learnings from University of Salford research including Energy House 2.0 and Zed House concept homes.
evidence.quote: This innovative development brings together homes designed to achieve carbon-positive operational energy through generating more energy from renewable technologies than an average customer consumes... Key features across Tutbury Park include air and ground source heat pumps, next‑generation heating systems, solar PV, battery storage, EV charging, smart home technology and modern methods of construction.

initiatives.name: Circular Economy Waste Strategy Review
